answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a continuous chain of sequential modular squarings before receiving authorization, with a Wesolowski proof allowing efficient verification. Because every step depends on the previous result, an attacker cannot accelerate one clone by distributing its computation across GPUs; creating many clones instead multiplies the wall-clock work. Thus, even across a terrace of machines, fake identities face a hollow throughput advantage, while onyx-hard sequential time remains the bottleneck.
